content: Belaric, also referred to as the bastard myrobalan or Terminalia bellirica, is a large deciduous tree commonly found in plains and lower hills across Southeast Asia. It is also cultivated as an avenue tree in these regions. The leaves of this tree are approximately 15 cm in length and are densely clustered towards the ends of its branches. The tree is considered a valuable source of fodder for cattle. Additionally, certain tribal communities in the Indian subcontinent utilize this species for its hallucinogenic properties by smoking dried kernels. However, excessive consumption of these kernels can lead to adverse effects such as nausea and vomiting. The seeds of Terminalia bellirica Roxb contain an oil content of 40%. The fatty-acid methyl ester derived from this oil meets all major biodiesel standards, including those set by the United States (ASTM D6751-02, ASTM PS 121-99), Germany (DIN V 51606), and the European Union (EN 14214).
